key_insight: A simple atom-extraction strategy called “deletions” outperforms more complex ways of carving out local atomic environments for DFT-based training data.
engineering_relevance: This work helps make active-learning and on-the-fly fitting of machine-learned interatomic potentials more practical by producing smaller periodic DFT-ready structures from large-scale simulations.
method: Benchmark multiple extraction shapes and sizes for local atomic environments.
Compare strategies for embedding extracted atoms into periodic DFT calculations, including passivation needs.
Evaluate a simple deletion-based procedure against alternative methods across diverse materials.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmarking on amorphous SiO2, Ta with screw dislocations, and molten C, with deletions showing superior performance across the tested cases.
watch_item: Results may depend on the material system, defect type, and how periodic-boundary-compatible extraction and passivation are implemented.
paper_title: Extracting Atomic Environments for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
